page: Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 1 vCPU, consisting of 1 physical core and 1 thread, running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1. Local storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core CPU performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2896.39, placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. However, because it is a single-core configuration, its multi-core stress-ng score is identical and ranks in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 130.9 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 20.94 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are also in the lower tiers, with a database operations score of 926.43 and a static web serving throughput of 1.44 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, yielding 27.17 GB/sec and 11.19 GB/sec respectively.

This server offers a qualitative balance of dedicated AMD CPU resources and a high memory allocation relative to its single core, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require more memory than compute power. The primary tradeoff is the single-thread limitation, which restricts multi-threaded scaling and results in lower throughput for database operations and web serving. It is best suited for lightweight memory-bound tasks, single-threaded processing, basic caching, or small-scale development environments.
